solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frenchwoman wearing Shilling hat's lost weight

parts.note: S is the old abbreviation for a shilling

indicators.note: something worn goes around its wearer, so one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame, a French married woman

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman in a shilling hat has dieted successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, worth twelve old pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim is to reduce one's body mass by dieting, so a person who slimmed has shed pounds.

clue.text: Most unhealthy model inspiring US fashion brand eats without stopping

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes others inside it

parts.note: to sit is to pose as a model for an artist
CK is Calvin Klein, the American fashion label

indicators.note: without its stopping means without its filling, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of eats

explanation.surface: A fashion model who keeps eating, inside an American designer's clothes, is in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' here means a filling, as in a tooth, so eats without it keeps only its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick means ill, and the superlative names the person in the poorest state of health.

clue.text: Fancy aircon, but bacteria may thrive in it

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine or elaborate, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Air conditioning is nice, but it can breed germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective for the air conditioning, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is a heated apparatus in which laboratory cultures of microbes are grown under controlled conditions.

clue.text: Part of Queen's Speech upset without intention

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue the letters then run bottom to top

parts.note: w/o is the written shorthand for without
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Part of the monarch's annual address to Parliament is unsettled and pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat. The Queen's Speech is the British monarch's address opening Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and a cat's characteristic vocal sound is a mewing cry.

clue.text: Moved away from infernal place where freemasons meet by day

parts.note: Dis is the underworld in Roman myth and Dante's Inferno
freemasons gather in a lodge
D is the abbreviation for day, placed by the rest

explanation.surface: Someone moved away from a hellish venue where freemasons gather in daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its fixed position, so it has been shifted.

clue.text: Pathetic (but not, ulimately, poignant) novel about an organ

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: relating to the liver

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
but not tells us a letter is to be left out of the word before it
ultimately (misspelt in the clue) points to the final letter of poignant

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A reviewer sniffs at a novel that is pathetic without ever quite being poignant, and happens to concern a bodily organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ulimately' takes T, the last letter of poignant; 'but not' drops a T from PATHETIC to leave PAHETIC, and 'novel' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatic is the medical adjective for anything concerning the liver, the body's largest internal organ.

clue.text: Boring transposition of halves of humble home

indicators.note: transposition means the two halves swap places, so the front part moves to the back

parts.note: the first half of each word: HUM from humble and HO from home

explanation.surface: It sounds like a dry grammar lesson about swapping parts of a modest house.
explanation.walkthrough: Take half of each word (HUM, HO), then 'transposition' swaps the two halves round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum is an informal adjective for something dull, routine and uninteresting.

clue.text: I'm occupying a chair adapted for posers

indicators.note: adapted means altered to fit, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a seat altered for people modelling for artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair' looks like furniture, but a chair is also a senior university post.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a professorship, so its holder is a senior academic.

clue.text: Extended family having no right, initially, to land

indicators.note: having no means a letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: a tribe is a large extended family group
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of to

explanation.surface: A large family without any legal entitlement to own territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a region on the Himalayan plateau, a country or territory in the sense of land.

clue.text: Russian cooks regularly given the boot

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of cooks
getting the boot or the sack both mean being dismissed

explanation.surface: Russian chefs who keep getting fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were a people of southern Russia and Ukraine famed as horsemen.

clue.text: Beverage companies against commonest feature of amalgamations

parts.note: two companies, each abbreviated CO
the letter that appears most often in the word amalgamations is A (four times)

explanation.surface: A drinks firm takes a stand against the usual pattern of corporate mergers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' just means next to. The A is a letter-counting trick: no other letter in amalgamations occurs as often.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao seeds mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: Transport fish in bulk at front of aircraft

parts.note: a school is a large group of fish swimming together
bus is pilots' slang for an aircraft

explanation.surface: An airline moves a large consignment of fish into the nose of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At front of' places the fish piece before the aircraft piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bus is a vehicle carrying pupils, so it is a form of conveyance for children.

clue.text: Freedom to perform Othello perhaps withdrawn by army section

parts.note: army read as arm-y, of the arm; the elbow is a section of the arm

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A regiment pulls out of a production of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army section' looks military but means part of the arm. 'By' sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move freely, figuratively the latitude to act as one wishes.

clue.text: Run a bit more

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball, such as a wide

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs gained from wides, no-balls and byes are counted separately from the batter's own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cricket score not off the bat, and also any additional amount beyond the usual.

clue.text: Revolutionary somewhat averse to teddy bears

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the letters run backwards
somewhat means only part, so the letters lie within the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of averse, to and the start of teddy

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who rather dislikes teddy bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teddy bears' looks like a single noun, but bears is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, so totes and bears are both third-person verbs for carrying.

clue.text: Crazy place to dance the twist?

parts.note: to screw is to twist
a ball is a formal dance event

explanation.surface: A wild venue where people do the Twist, the 1960s dance craze.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twist was a 1960s dance, so 'dance the twist' reads as one phrase; here the twist is a separate piece placed before the dance venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric person, and as an adjective it means zany or mad.

clue.text: Guides losing heart arriving at factory back to front? That's speculation

indicators.note: arriving at means the first part comes up against the second, so one is set right after the other
losing heart means the central letters of the word are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back to front means the last letter is brought round to the start

parts.note: a factory is works

explanation.surface: Girl Guides arrive at a factory in a muddle and are left guessing.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of a six-letter word is its middle two letters, ID here; 'back to front' moves the last letter of the factory word to its start, and 'arriving at' joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Guesswork is the process of reaching conclusions by guessing, which is what speculation is.

clue.text: Football sides scoffing extremely saccharine refreshments

indicators.note: scoffing means wolfing down, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, so a side is an eleven

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: the outer letters of saccharine

explanation.surface: Football teams gobbling sugary snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion falls just before the final letter of the sides. Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack break.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light mid-morning snack with tea or coffee, taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Different white rose cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated means grown and worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinctive white rose bred by a gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, otherwise means other than supposed, so in a different state or way.

clue.text: Case of recurring Xmas present being given fresh introduction

indicators.note: a fresh introduction means the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, a partridge in a pear tree is given again in every verse

explanation.surface: Someone gets the same Christmas gift every year, now with a new opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not separately clued; the definition steers it to C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing that holds ammunition, ink or film, so it is a kind of container.

clue.text: What setters do in school on French island

definitions.note: a phrase describing an activity, standing for the verb

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Crossword setters at work in a school on an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the school above the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters assemble grids and clues, and compiler is the trade term for a puzzle setter.

clue.text: Swimmer about to spend time drying out?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards
to spend something is to use it up, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a bather is someone who swims
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A swimmer is about to spend time getting dry after leaving the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drying out' looks like towelling off, but it means giving up alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is treatment for addiction, and drying out is the idiom for an alcoholic getting sober.

clue.text: Confused birds overwhelmed by garden plot

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a bed is a plot of ground in a garden
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Bewildered birds swamped in a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled or bewildered, unable to understand what is going on.

clue.text: Bird starts to make awful crow-like noise

indicators.note: starts point to the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of make and awful
caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A bird starts squawking horribly like a crow.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America.

clue.text: Liberal in bed with hot cleaner

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician caught in bed with a sweaty cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person, but it is the thing used for wiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth is a piece of fabric used for wiping and dusting surfaces, so it is a cleaning item.

clue.text: Swirling stream, primarily menacing or life-threatening?

definitions.text: Swirling stream, primarily menacing or life-threatening?

indicators.note: swirling means moving round in eddies, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the words whose first letters are taken
first letter of life-threatening, the hyphenated word counted as one under primarily

explanation.surface: A description of a dangerous whirlpool, the kind that might drown you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes MO from menacing and or, plus L from life-threatening; 'Swirling' mixes them in with STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a violently swirling body of water that can be deadly to ships.

clue.text: Second dictionary supports derivative of bovine expression

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A second dictionary backs up the origin of a cow-related phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supports' puts the dictionary underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Moo is a cow's lowing sound, and its past tense is a form derived from that word.

clue.text: American man's recycled food from the East

indicators.note: recycled suggests going round again, so the letters are rotated from the end to the start

parts.note: US is short for American
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: An American recycles Asian food packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: USHIS is rotated, moving its last four letters to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, Japan being in the Far East.

clue.text: They segregate active political prisoners without principle, unfortunately

definitions.note: plural, matching the plural noun: those who keep things apart

indicators.note: active means busy or in motion, so the letters of political prisoners are stirred up
without tells us the letters of principle are removed from that mix
unfortunately pairs with active as a second signal that the letters end up in a different, unlucky order

explanation.surface: A complaint that politically active prisoners are being treated without principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the letters of PRINCIPLE from POLITICAL PRISONERS, and 'active ... unfortunately' signals that the nine letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolators are people or devices that separate things off, keeping them apart from others.

clue.text: Scouts' special food

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
pies are a kind of food

explanation.surface: The particular dish served at a Scout camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scouts’' looks like a possessive noun, but it is a verb: reconnoitres.
explanation.definitionFit: To scout is to reconnoitre secretly, and to spy is to watch covertly to gather information.

clue.text: Former news chief, bored by prince, sighed

indicators.note: something bored by a drill has a hole made in it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: EX means former and ED is an editor, the chief of a newspaper
Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: An ex-editor groaned at being bored by a tedious royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former news chief' is one piece, a former editor, which the prince then drills into.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh is to breathe out audibly, and to exhale is to breathe out, so they match in sense and tense.

clue.text: Pay band essentially lacking limit

indicators.note: lacking its essence means the central letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: a strip is a narrow band
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: A salary band that, at heart, has no upper limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay band' reads as a salary grade, but pay is the definition and band is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular sum paid as a salary or allowance, especially to clergy or students.
